subject.title: Wear OS companion via phone-proxy architecture

question: Should Wear OS v1 be formally constrained to a first-party phone-proxy architecture in which the watch stores no gateway credentials and cannot connect directly to the gateway?
rationale: The issue proposes a sensible boundary, but a new paired-device RPC and release surface requires explicit Android/product ownership of the permanent authorization model before implementation proceeds.

options.title: Approve phone-proxy-only v1
options.body: Proceed with staged PRs that keep gateway authentication on the phone and expose only a typed, bounded, explicitly allowlisted watch RPC.

options.title: Defer until Android hardening completes
options.body: Keep the design open but postpone implementation until current Android background, security, notification, and release work is considered sufficiently mature.

options.title: Design standalone watch access
options.body: Broaden the scope to direct gateway connectivity, requiring a separate credential, TLS, identity, migration, and recovery design before coding.

recommendation.title: Approve phone-proxy-only v1
recommendation.body: Proceed with staged PRs that keep gateway authentication on the phone and expose only a typed, bounded, explicitly allowlisted watch RPC.
